text: The word of the LORD came to me:
What do you mean by repeating this proverb about the land of Israel: "The fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge"?
As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you shall no longer use this proverb in Israel.
See, every soul belongs to me: the soul of the father as well as the soul of the son is mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
Suppose a man is righteous and does what is just and right.
He does not eat at the mountain shrines or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor's wife or approach a woman during her period.
He oppresses no one; he returns what he took in pledge for a debt; he commits no robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.

versions.text: He oppresses no one, but returns the pledge he holds for a debt. He commits no robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
versions.explanation: The conjunction "but" creates a false contrast between not oppressing and returning a pledge. A simple series of clauses matches the Hebrew list and flows better when read aloud.

text: He does not lend at interest or take a profit. He holds back his hand from wrongdoing and judges fairly between one person and another.
He walks in my statutes and faithfully keeps my ordinances. Such a man is righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord GOD.
But suppose he has a violent son, who sheds blood and does any of these things
—he does none of these good things, but instead eats at the mountain shrines and defiles his neighbor's wife,

versions.text: —though the father did none of them: the son eats at the mountain shrines, defiles his neighbor's wife,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew subject "וְהוּא" most naturally refers to the son just introduced in v.10, and "כָּל־אֵלֶּה" points back to the righteous deeds of vv.5–9: the son does none of them, "for indeed" (כִּי גַם) he eats at the mountain shrines. The current rendering shifts the subject to the father, which adds an interpretation not in the text and breaks the logic of the contrast introduced by כִּי גַם.

text: oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return a pledge, lifts up his eyes to the idols, and does what is detestable,

versions.text: oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return a pledge, lifts up his eyes to the idols, commits abomination,
versions.explanation: "Commits abomination" is stiff for oral reading and inconsistent with v.13, where תּוֹעֵבוֹת is rendered "detestable things." A consistent, natural rendering aids the ear.

text: lends at interest and takes a profit. Will he live? He will not live! Because he has done all these detestable things, he shall surely be put to death; his blood will be on his own head.
But suppose this man in turn has a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, and though he sees them, he does not do the same.
He does not eat at the mountain shrines or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor's wife.
He oppresses no one, takes no pledge, commits no robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
He holds back his hand from harming the poor, takes no interest or profit, keeps my ordinances and walks in my statutes. He will not die for his father's guilt; he will surely live.
But his father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was not good among his people—he will die for his own guilt.
Yet you ask, "Why should the son not bear his father's guilt?" Since the son has done what is just and right, keeping all my statutes and carrying them out, he will surely live.

The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear his father's guilt, nor will a father bear his son's guilt. The righteousness of the righteous will be his own, and the wickedness of the wicked will be his own.
But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all my statutes, and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die.
None of the transgressions he has committed will be remembered against him. Because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord GOD. Is it not rather that he turn from his ways and live?

But if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, committing the same detestable things the wicked man does, will he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done will be remembered. Because of the treachery he is guilty of and the sin he has committed, he will die.
Yet you say, "The Lord's way is not fair." Listen, house of Israel: Is my way unfair? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die for it; because of the wrong he has done, he will die.
And if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life.
Because he considered and turned away from all the transgressions he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
Yet the house of Israel says, "The Lord's way is not fair." Are my ways unfair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each one according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Repent! Turn away from all your transgressions, so that guilt will not be your downfall.
Cast away from you all the transgressions you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, house of Israel?
For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, declares the Lord GOD. So turn, and live!
